manual: A war that runs for weeks with fighting: the dead of both sides against the war overview's casualties
A real alliance war (the Allies): several enemies joining over days, one of them capitulating while the war goes on
An existing save of the build before E4 round 2 with finished and running wars: the migration (rows grouped, dead not kept, leaders from the Government page)
Commanders who took states and points in a war: they need fighting, or mod1440_chk_state2 with a general in the state
checklist: E7 with Road to 56: in the file of the war with Poland after mod1440_chk_e7_take (and a day), the faces under 'Our commanders in this war' are each general's own, the same as in his army's leader view (34x46); mod1440_chk_e7_log: 'war k 1 ...'
E7: a file with fewer than five commanders shows no face on the empty lines; a war with none shows only 'None of your generals ...'

The page in the steel look: three steel cards in the left column (The campaign 548x220, Wars of today 548x188, Finished wars 548x670), 6 apart, each with a head band of 27 holding its title and the column heads (Days / Our dead / Their dead / Surr.; Began / Our dead / Their dead / End); the window's ground, title strip and tabs unchanged; the Wars tab's tooltip 'One row per war, its enemies joined'

The campaign table: 14 figures in two columns, bands on rows 2, 4, 6. Compare 'Casualties, all wars' with National Figures' 'Casualties, all wars'; 'in wars of today' with the war overview's casualties of your side; Our surrender with the war overview's bar; 'Casualties we inflicted' with the sum of Their dead over both lists

Declare war on Poland (effect mod1440_chk_war), run 3 days: one red plate under Wars of today with Poland's flag and name, Days 3, Our dead and Their dead in K with one decimal, Surr. as the war overview's capitulation bar of Poland; 'At peace.' gone

Grouping (has_war_together_with): effect mod1440_chk_ally_join (the United Kingdom and France join Poland's side), run 1 day: still ONE plate, 'Poland +2'; effect mod1440_chk_wr_log: game.log 'MOD1440 wr: row' gives POL, ENG and FRA the same grp and role 1. Then mod1440_chk_war2 (Czechoslovakia, a war of its own): a second plate, its own grp

The file of the war: 'The war with Poland', both flags, 'German Reich' and 'Poland +2' in hoi_24header, '1 January, 1936 - today - N days'; the track and its marks; Their side '3 enemies'; the enemies table, 3 rows (flag, name, Joined, surrender %, Their dead, Our dead, States), Poland on the lighter band; click the United Kingdom: its row lights and Their side shows its head of government (Chamberlain)

Casualties (casualties_inflicted_by, faults 1 and 3): after some days of fighting, mod1440_chk_wr_log: each row's kus/kthem and 'now' readings in thousands; compare a one-enemy war's Our dead and Their dead with the war overview's casualties of each participant (the difference: the dead no enemy caused) and write both numbers down; the plate, the file's 'Casualties, by their hand / by our hand' and the enemies table's columns agree with the sums

meta_trigger with numbers from variables: after Reloading Database and a daily round, error.log has no line about meta_trigger, casualties_inflicted_by, a '[N]' or '[O]' placeholder or a parse error; mod1440_chk_kread_time: the time of 100 full readings between two game.log lines

The peace (mod1440_chk_peace: white peace with Poland), run 1 day: Poland's row leaves the war of today if the war goes on, or the war moves to Finished wars on a blue plate with the peace icon; Our dead and Their dead keep the values of the day before, NOT 0 (fault 1); mod1440_chk_wr_log after the peace: the 'now' reading tells whether casualties_inflicted_by keeps its value after a peace or falls to 0 (write it down)

A second war with Poland after the peace (mod1440_chk_war again, 2 days): a plate of its own; its dead count from its first day (the reading of that day is its base, kus0 in the log); the first war's file keeps its numbers, and its War Diary lines stop at its last day (designer's fault 3)

Kept heads of government (fault 2): during a war, mod1440_chk_leader_change (Poland's head of government retired), run 1 day: Poland's row keeps the head of the first day (lt0) and the new one (lt1) in mod1440_chk_wr_log; its file shows 'At the start' and 'Today', two portraits. After the peace, mod1440_chk_leader_change_us (ours retired): the finished war still shows our head of that time, 'Throughout the war', one portrait

An annexed enemy (mod1440_chk_war2, mod1440_chk_annex, 1 day): a green plate with the annex icon; its file still shows Czechoslovakia's head of government at the start and the end with his portrait (no 'This country is no more')
The flag box: a head of government the game has no portrait for shows the country's flag (82x52) on the dark inset with the ideology icon under it, tooltip 'No portrait the game can name'

A finished war of one enemy: no enemies table; the War Diary runs from the left column (10 lines) into the right one (up to 21 lines, 'In the War Diary, continued'); 'How it ended' in the fourth figure row with the outcome's words
'All its lines' in the War Diary strip: the War Diary opens filtered to the chosen enemy ('<country>: lines 1 - N of N')
A place in the file's War Diary is a button: the camera moves to it and the Records close

Migration of an existing save: effect mod1440_chk_old4 (the rows as the build before left them), open the Records: game.log 'the rows of wr ... wo were given their wars, casualties and leaders'; mod1440_chk_sizes4 logs every new part as long as the rows; the old finished wars show the dash in both dead slots (tooltip 'Not kept'), an enemy fought once and not at war now may show the game's value instead; rows that ended on the same day are one plate; our heads of government come from the Government page, theirs 'Not recorded' at the start
The lists scroll with the wheel: Finished wars past 12 plates, the enemies table past 5 rows

error.log: no line that names the mod, no 'invalid scope for var', no 'Could not find sprite type' (GFX_1440p_WR_*, GFX_1440p_SG_inset_125x168), no unknown trigger or effect has_war_together_with, has_offensive_war_with, casualties_inflicted_by, is_subject_of
